nodes.label: TimerScheduler (context.timers)
nodes.rationale: Tied to the actor instance and auto-cancels on stop and on restart, so a restarted actor never inherits stale timers. Timers are keyed by string (same key replaces, no duplicate fires) and fire by tell to self, so the work is serialized with the actor's other messages, supervised, and visible in traces. The default choice for ~90% of timer code.

nodes.label: Scheduler (system.scheduler)
nodes.rationale: Tied to the actor system, so it survives any actor stop or restart. Three legitimate uses: initiating work from outside the actor world (a SIGTERM handler), work that must outlive a specific actor, and framework code with no actor context. Its Function variants catch and log throws but do not escalate.

nodes.label: Cancellable
nodes.rationale: Returned by every scheduler method; cancel() returns true only if it actually cancelled an active schedule, false if it had already fired or been cancelled.

nodes.label: ManualScheduler
nodes.rationale: Implements the same Scheduler interface but only advances time on advance(ms), because real-time waiting in tests is flaky, slow and order-dependent. It plugs into context.timers too via the system's Scheduler injection.

nodes.label: Fixed-rate semantics
nodes.rationale: scheduleAtFixedRate does not chase missed firings and does not compress them either — a backed-up mailbox simply accumulates ticks. Missed-firing detection is left to the actor recording its own last-fire timestamp; there is no built-in mode.

nodes.label: Raw setTimeout async escape
nodes.rationale: Raw setTimeout/setInterval callbacks run outside the actor's message-processing turn: throws bypass supervision entirely and the callback can fire after the actor stopped, operating on a destroyed cell. context.timers.startSingleTimer turns the fire into an ordinary supervised, stop-safe message to self.

nodes.label: High-frequency timers as mailbox pressure
nodes.rationale: A timer interval shorter than the worst-case handler latency grows the mailbox without bound, and mailboxes are unbounded, so it grows until the heap does. Pick an interval slower than worst-case latency or bound the mailbox and accept dropped ticks.
